labs.title: Read the OPTIONS
labs.prompt: Dissect the OPTIONS. The CSeq method token has to match the request line.

labs.title: Dissect the phone URI
labs.prompt: Find the URI parameter that marks the user part as a phone number.

labs.title: Name the codec document
labs.prompt: The offer uses static payload 0. Identify which recommendation defines that codec.

labs.title: Dissect a debug INVITE
labs.prompt: The capture bench strips the debug prefix. Read the branch and the missing To tag.

labs.title: Class the code
labs.prompt: Dissect the final response in this lab message, which is the 486.

labs.title: Rewrite From on purpose
labs.prompt: Run the profile. It is legal syntax and a dangerous edit. See which URI the From header contains afterward.

labs.title: Find the dialog id
labs.prompt: Dissect the 180. List the three values that identify the early dialog.

labs.title: Read the teaching config
labs.prompt: The config is a dial-peer, a trusted source, an empty profile, and one debug command.

labs.title: Put lr back
labs.prompt: The header-rule matches a Record-Route that lost lr and writes the parameter back.

labs.title: Check RAck
labs.prompt: Dissect the PRACK. Separate RAck from CSeq.

labs.title: Negotiate the second offer
labs.prompt: The UPDATE offer adds a port change and still lists PCMU and PCMA. The answer keeps PCMU.

labs.title: Read the 422
labs.prompt: The response tells you the floor. The next INVITE has to meet it.

labs.title: Dissect a BYE
labs.prompt: This BYE assumes the dialog already exists. Find the CSeq and the To tag.

labs.title: Read Refer-To
labs.prompt: Find the Replaces parameter inside Refer-To. It is escaped.

labs.title: Read the 423
labs.prompt: The registrar rejected the interval. The header you need is Min-Expires.

labs.title: Count the flows
labs.prompt: Dissect the second 200 OK. Two Contact headers share an instance and differ by reg-id.

labs.title: Which header is outbound?
labs.prompt: The 200 OK has both Path and Service-Route. Pick the one the UA will preload.

labs.title: Find both GRUUs
labs.prompt: The 200 OK Contact carries pub-gruu and temp-gruu.

labs.title: Point at c= and m=
labs.prompt: Dissect the INVITE and find the connection line and both media lines.

labs.title: Negotiate two m-lines
labs.prompt: Run the negotiator. The answer refuses the second stream without deleting it.

labs.title: Match opus on the name
labs.prompt: The offer says payload 96 opus. The answer says payload 111 opus. G722/8000 is on payload 9 on both sides.

labs.title: Answer a hold
labs.prompt: The offer is sendonly. A legal answer is recvonly. Negotiate and read the direction line.

labs.title: See a zero port
labs.prompt: Negotiate an offer of two audio lines. The answer accepts the first and zeros the second.

labs.title: 183 has SDP, 180 does not
labs.prompt: Extract both responses. One progress message has SDP and the ringing message does not.

labs.title: Find the delayed offer
labs.prompt: This INVITE has an empty body. Decide where the offer is allowed to appear.

labs.title: Find where the header is not
labs.prompt: Dissect the 200 OK. The body names a port. The RTP header is not one of the SIP headers.

labs.title: Read static types
labs.prompt: The offer lists PCMU and PCMA on separate m-lines. Confirm the clocks are 8000.

labs.title: See opus survive a new payload type
labs.prompt: Negotiate the offer and answer. Confirm opus matches across payload types 96 and 111, and that G722 stays at 8000.
